IMPORTANT PIN CAVEAT: the KCR is a rail service/route, and no OSM element maps the route or the service as a whole (Overpass relation name~'Circular' and 'KCR' queries in the Karachi bbox return nothing). The pin used is the OSM node named 'Nipa Station Karachi Circular Railway' - a KCR-named station element that is itself tagged amenity=bus_station (the Nipa station building, whose rail use is superseded/repurposed per OSM tagging) - so the coordinates identify a KCR station in Gulshan-e-Iqbal, NOT the corridor. The catalogue's address 'KCR Road, Saddar to Landhi' could not be confirmed against any OSM element. No official KCR website was found (no *.gov.pk service site located from here; Pakistan Railways site not specific to KCR), so hours/fares/contact are null; Wikipedia explicitly notes the revived service's status instead (kept in description). Photo shows a KCR train at Karachi City Railway Station per its file-page caption.

PIN/ADDRESS DISCREPANCY flagged: the only OSM element named 'Karachi Grammar School' (node 5330850896, amenity=school) sits in North Nazimabad (Buffer Zone Sector 16-A), while the official website footer states the school address as Plot ST-20, Khayaban-e-Saadi, Clifton Block 5, Karachi 75600, and the English Wikipedia page carries yet another coordinate (24.8648, 67.0284 - the historic Saddar-era location per the article's map). Wikipedia's 'three sites' statement suggests multiple campuses, so which campus a visitor means is genuinely ambiguous; the OSM pin is published with its own road, and the official Clifton address is kept verbatim, with the mismatch recorded here rather than papered over. No phone or email appears on the fetched official pages (footer carries address only), so contact is null and confidence stays partially-verified despite the official site resolving. Commons has no file that names Karachi Grammar School ('File:KGS JS.jpg' is ambiguous and not verifiably the school - photo null). Note: the catalogue's own address ('St. Thomas's Road, Clifton Block 1') matches none of the sources checked and should not be relied on.

Here the venue IS the KMC head office, so unlike the Frere Hall / Empress Market records in batch-f, publishing the site's own head-office hours ('Opening Hours: Mon-Fri 9:00am-5:00pm', printed in the kmc.gos.pk footer) and phone/email is correct attribution rather than misattribution; Saturday/Sunday are left with open:null because the footer states only Mon-Fri. Pin: Nominatim zoom-19 reverse geocode at the Wikipedia building coordinates (24.8554, 67.0077, taken from the 'Karachi Metropolitan Corporation Building' article only to locate the search, not published) lands exactly on OSM way 526478282, whose OSM name is misspelled 'Karachi Muncipal Corporation Building' - kept verbatim in the address string. The kmc.gos.pk homepage carries a 'We're currently working on updating our website' placeholder banner. Commons file caption reads 'Karachi Municipal Corporation (KMC) Head Office' and the file page flags it as a protected Pakistani monument (SD-P-16).

The official Mall Timings page gives different hours per section: retail outlets Sun-Thu 11:00-23:00, Fri 15:00-24:00, Sat 11:00-24:00 (used for the per-day hours array, marked '(retail outlets)'); Food Court Sun-Thu 12:00-24:00 and Fri-Sat 12:00-01:00; Onederland Mon-Thu 12:00-23:00, Fri 14:00-24:00, Sat 11:00-24:00, Sun 11:00-23:00; Carrefour Sun-Thu 10:00-24:00, Fri-Sat 10:00-01:00; TriFit Mon-Sat 06:00-23:00, Sun 10:00-19:00 - the non-retail sections are summarised here rather than flattened into the hours array. Phone (+92) 21 36321311 and info@luckyone.com.pk are printed on the timings page itself ('NEED INFORMATION? CALL: (+92) 21 36321311') as the mall's own line (the contact page also lists a corporate landline (+92) 21 3632 2586 with office hours 'Monday To Friday - 10AM To 07PM' - the corporate office line, deliberately not used as the venue contact). Entry is free to walk in but no official page states a ticket price, so ticketPrices is null. Commons photo caption: 'Outside view at night' of Lucky One Mall (May 2020).

sources.url: https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter (node[name~"Tooba"] in Karachi bbox via maps.mail.ru mirror; result: node 12134251807)

notes.text: Node 12134251807 (amenity=place_of_worship, religion=muslim, name 'Tooba Masjid') sits at 24.8433, 67.0541, which matches the English Wikipedia article's coordinate (24.8430, 67.0544) to within about 50 m, confirming it is THIS mosque; a second, different 'Jamia Masjid Tooba' (node 4764688490) exists near Lyari and was excluded. The catalogue's address ('DHA Phase 5, near the sea face') matches no checked source and should be replaced by the OSM/Wikipedia wording above; note OSM/Nominatim place it on Old Korangi Road under Saddar Town administration while Wikipedia says DHA Phase II - the boundary line runs through the area, both strings are reproduced verbatim. No managing body publishes hours, fees or visitor rules on any fetched official page (a working mosque opens for prayers, not visiting hours), so those fields are null; entryConditions left null because the only sources are descriptive (Wikipedia), not operator rules. Photo is from A.Savin's 2020 Karachi set; its file-page caption names the Tooba Mosque explicitly.

OSM AMBIGUITY: three Karachi elements claim the name - way 1178255967 (leisure=stadium, centre 24.8952, 67.0817, Essa Nagri Block 17), node 5091305056 (leisure=stadium, 'National Stadium, Karachi', Stadium Road, KDA Scheme 1 Extension, 24.8928, 67.0829) and way 480397211 (leisure=pitch, 24.8961, 67.0814). The Wikidata coordinate for 'National Stadium, Karachi' (Q3007369) is 24.8961, 67.0814, closest to the pitch/stadium polygon in Block 17, so way 1178255967 is published as the pin with the caveat that the Stadium-Road node lies ~350 m away (the old ground footprint vs the redeveloped complex may explain the split - unverified). No official venue page (PCB or Sindh Sports Board) publishing standing hours or a tariff was found; the PCB's own press release for the 28 April 2025 qualifier (fetched in search listing only, pcb.com.pk) lists a match-day ticket of PKR 500 for all enclosures - event-specific, so it is recorded here as PRESS-style secondary context and kept OUT of ticketPrices per rules. Entry conditions (bag checks, gates opening match-day only) are unverified and omitted. Photo filename and caption name the National Stadium, Karachi (September 2021).

Pin: OSM has no single university-boundary element for the main campus; the named elements are individual campus buildings - way 376064879 'NED University (Admin Block)' (24.9327, 67.1103) and way 376064880 'NED University (Library)' on NED Circular Road, Gulshan-e-Iqbal, which sit at the coordinate given by Wikipedia's article (24.9318, 67.1126), i.e. the Main Campus; a separate 'NED University (City Campus)' building way (789869567, Dr. Ziauddin Road, Civil Lines) matches the site's City Campus address and was NOT used for the pin. The catalogue's address ('University Road, near Manghopir, Saddar') is a garbled mix and was replaced by the official Contact-Us strings. Contact (main-campus phone range and registrar@neduet.edu.pk) is printed on the official site, hence verified - but it is the registrar's office line, not a public visitor line, and the university publishes no visiting hours, so hours stays null. Earlier guesses nedu.edu.pk / ned.edu.pk are NXDOMAIN on public resolvers; the live official domain is www.neduet.edu.pk.

sources.url: https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter (name~"1122" and fire_station/ambulance queries in Karachi bbox via maps.mail.ru mirror; result: node 12227788485)

notes.text: PIN CAVEAT: there is no OSM element for 'Rescue 1122 Sindh/Karachi headquarters' (Overpass searches for 'Rescue 1122', '1122', amenity=fire_station and emergency=ambulance_station across the Karachi bbox returned exactly one Karachi 1122 element); node 12227788485 is a single named station ('SIEHS-1122 North Nazimabad Station (7)') and the coordinates describe that station, not the service area. The official site rescue1122.org is a JavaScript app; its served HTML carries the 1122 emergency number in title/meta text ('Rescue1122 Emergency Services'), which is the only contact value published - no email and no Karachi line printed, so email is null and confidence stays partially-verified (a hotline, not a venue contact/timetable). The catalogue's 'Stations across all seven districts' was not verifiable from official pages. Commons photo explicitly names 'RESCUE 1122' but shows the Okara (Punjab) station, not a Karachi one - kept because the record subject is the Rescue 1122 service itself, with this caveat published rather than implying a Karachi scene.

Pin is the large OSM campus way (amenity=university, name:en 'University of Karachi'), centre 24.9437, 67.1206, matching Wikipedia's coordinate (~24.94, 67.12). The official homepage footer/contact block prints 'Address: University Road, Karachi-75270' and 'Email: registrar@uok.edu.pk' - a registrar office email rather than a public visitor contact, and no phone number or visiting hours appear in the fetchable HTML (the site is partly JS-rendered), so phone is null and the record is marked verified only on the strength of the printed venue email; if the generator treats registrar email as insufficient, this is a candidate for downgrade to partially-verified. Catalogue address 'Stadium Road, Gulshan-e-Iqbal' conflicts with the official 'University Road' and was replaced. Commons photo names the campus's Silver Jubilee Gate explicitly (November 2022).

The police emergency contact directory prints 'Madadgar-15' for the emergency line and, beside the Karachi Police entry, the address line 'Karachi Cantonment Fowler Lines, Shahrah-e-Faisal, Karachi' - quoted as served, with the city suffix removed so it reads as an address. The Commissioner Karachi's own emergency-services page lists 'Madadgar Police: 15' independently, so the number is double-sourced. The same police page lists Zainab Alert on 1099, which is the only women's helpline number either page publishes (the older 109 is not printed on either and is therefore not published here). No street address, telephone line, email, opening hours or tariff is published for a complaint office or a missing-person unit on either page, so those stay null rather than being inferred from the record name; the contact here is the city-wide emergency number, not a switchboard.

Both government pages publish the fire number independently: the Commissioner Karachi's emergency-services page prints 'KMC Fire Brigade: 16' and the police emergency contact directory prints 'Fire Brigade 16'. Neither page publishes a station address, a switchboard number, an email, hours or a fee, and no street address for the brigade was verified from an official source, so address is null - the seeded 'Station across Saddar, SITE, Malir' line described a network rather than a location and is removed. The record publishes the number a caller needs and nothing else.

The Accident & Emergency page states verbatim: 'The service is provided 24 hours a day, 365 days per year.' and prints the emergency numbers 021-34412245 & 021-34412445 plus the address 'Stadium Road, Karachi 74800, Pakistan'. Only the emergency department's round-the-clock hours are recorded; the OPD timetable is not published on either fetched page. Nominatim returns two Karachi features named 'Liaquat National Hospital' — the main Stadium Road hospital (relation/17336275, used here, matching the published address) and a separate building in Nazimabad (node/5079542899) — so the pin is the Stadium Road campus.

exclusions.reason: The entry price circulating for this place came from the operator’s own social posts, where the amount contradicted its own label (“Rs. 1,000 (Rs. 500 redeemable)”). No tariff page could be read, so no price is published.

OpenStreetMap maps one Rescue station (SIEHS-1122 North Nazimabad Station 7), not the service. Pinning the city-wide Rescue 1122 record to that one station, or printing its street as the service’s address, would claim a verified headquarters that no source states — so the record keeps only the 1122 number, which is the thing the reader actually needs.

The only Karachi node OpenStreetMap names “Karachi Grammar School” sits in North Nazimabad, while the school’s own published address is Clifton Block 5 (the campus has three sites). The mismatch is recorded in the research notes; until one of the two is shown to be the senior school, no verified pin is published for it.
